title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Pet and house sitting
audience: Pet and house sitters who want repeat bookings and referrals from owners they have already looked after.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the client confirms the result and that the client can decline easily.
Write a next-service offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the condition for payment, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask once the owner is satisfied
instruction.body: The best time to ask for a review or referral is after the owner has confirmed the stay went well, usually at handover or when the final payment clears. Ask in one sentence, name the step you want (a review, or the name of one person who might need a sitter) and make it easy to say no. Record what you asked and the reply. One experiment found that a late reminder brought in more reviews than an immediate one, but it was a single study and not an Australian one (Baylor Keller Center, 1 June 2024). Google provides a review link or QR code that you can share. Never write reviews for owners, invent them, or ask only owners you expect to be happy: a vendor source describes that as review gating, which Google treats as a violation (Podium, 2 May 2022). Google also bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews (Google Business Profile Help, no date shown), and the ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says (ACCC, 15 July 2026).

instruction.heading: Offer the next stay before the owner leaves
instruction.body: Propose the next stay with dates, the same scope and a price approach, and write it down. Confirm the owner agrees before you change any diary. The research found no Australian figure for repeat house-sitting or repeat-booking rates, so do not assume how often owners return. If the offer goes by email or text, check the electronic message rules first. ACMA's guidance says inferred consent is narrow and does not cover a message sent just after a purchase (ACMA, no date shown).

instruction.heading: Check in at a set interval
instruction.body: A short check-in after about ninety days is a starting point to test, not a benchmark. Ask whether the arrangement still suits, whether anything has changed, and whether there is other work to quote. A message that only asks about the pets may not be commercial, but a message that promotes any service can be commercial, even when it is framed as a reminder (Clayton Utz, 9 November 2023). Check the rule before you send.

instruction.heading: Re-contact owners before their busy periods
instruction.body: Plan a short message before periods you can see in your own bookings, such as school holidays or a long trip you know about from earlier stays. No Australian source for holiday or seasonal demand for pet sitting was found, so set the dates from your own calendar. Offer the slots you can deliver, on written terms, with a clear way to opt out. ACMA says an unsubscribe must be honoured within five working days (ACMA, no date shown), so record each opt-out as soon as you receive it.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: Decide the reward, such as a credit on the next stay, and write down the payment condition, which is normally that the referred owner completes a paid stay. Give the referrer a copy. In seven studies, stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals (Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research, 2023). Get the referred person's consent before any referral message is sent (Clayton Utz, 2017; an older source). No business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found, so the tax and contract effect of a reward is UNCONFIRMED. Check any cash reward with an adviser.

procedure: After each stay is handed over, make one review or referral request and record the request and the reply.
Write the next-stay offer with dates, scope, visit times and price approach, and confirm it with the owner.
Schedule a check-in about ninety days after the stay, and send it under the electronic message rules.
Plan re-contact dates from your own calendar, and exclude anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward and its payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referred owner completes a paid stay, apply the reward and record the outcome.

workedExamples.situation: A sitter has looked after an owner's two dogs for a week while the owner travelled for work. At handover, the owner says she would recommend the sitter to her sister, who lives nearby and travels often. The sitter would like to offer a credit on the next stay if the sister books.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the sitter write down before the sister books, and what should she avoid?
workedExamples.reasoning: She writes the credit, the payment condition (the sister completes a paid stay) and the date the credit is applied, and gives the owner a copy. She asks the owner to pass on the sister's details, and contacts the sister only if she agrees. She does not promise a reward she has not written down. If she is unsure of the tax or contract effect of a credit, she checks with an adviser. A referral does not extend her insurance or any permit or registration she holds, so she accepts only the stays her cover and the local rules allow.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the stay dates, the handover date and the review or referral request made
Next-stay offer template with dates, scope and price approach
Calendar of re-contact dates built from your own bookings
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any home visit follows the owner's home safety notes

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the owner has said the stay went well
commonErrors.prevention: Ask at handover or at payment.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing an owner's name, photo or details of the home without consent
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting an owner who asked not to hear from you
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list, honour it at once, and keep messages factual and optional.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing an owner's name, photo, review or property details needs the owner's consent for that use. Do not write reviews for an owner or invent them. Owner details may be personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) if it applies to your business. Check the OAIC small business guidance to see whether it applies.

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own incentive rules. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews, and the ACCC says incentives must be disclosed. Check each platform's rules before you offer a reward.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). The Spam Act text was not read for this research, so check it before sending.

A referral does not extend your licence, registration, permit or insurance. Victorian rules for in-home pet sitting are UNRESOLVED, so accept only the stays your cover and the rules where the work happens allow.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after the stay is confirmed as satisfactory, and includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-stay offer is written, dated and confirmed by the owner before the diary changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log, with the date and the reply
Next-stay offers with dates, scope, visit times and owner confirmation
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after handover, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next stay in writing, with dates, before the owner leaves.
Set referral rewards and their payment conditions in writing before anyone refers.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask an owner for a review or referral?
options: Before the stay starts, so the owner feels committed
After the owner has confirmed the stay went well
Only when the owner has sent you a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: An owner wants to post a review with her name and a photo of the home. What do you need?
options: Her consent for the name and photo you plan to publish
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the photo looks professional

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred owner books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the payment condition stated

ACCC, 'Online reviews for product and services', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/advertising-and-promotions/online-reviews-for-product-and-services, published and updated 15 July 2026.

Podium, 'Review gating', https://www.podium.com/article/review-gating, 2 May 2022. Vendor source; the Google position was not checked against Google's own policy.

Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research 60(2), 2023, https://research.polyu.edu.hk/en/publications/i-will-get-a-reward-too-when-disclosing-the-referrer-reward-incre/. Stating the referrer reward in the invitation; no figures used.
Clayton Utz, 'Referrer beware', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2017/may/referrer-beware-proceed-with-caution-when-contemplating-refer-a-friend-promotions, 11 May 2017. Older than 2022.

Clayton Utz, 'The ACMA cranks up enforcement', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2023/november/the-acma-cranks-up-enforcement-do-your-factual-customer-emails-pass-the-spam-act-test, 9 November 2023.
ACMA, 'Avoid sending spam', https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, no date shown; read 2026-11-03 or 2026-11-04 per the research file.
Gap: no Australian data on repeat house-sitting or referral rates was found. The Baylor figure is from one experiment and is not an Australian rate.
Gap: no business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found; the tax and contract effect of rewards is UNCONFIRMED.
Victorian in-home pet sitting rules: UNRESOLVED in the team4 pet-care research file.

officialReferences.title: ACMA, Avoid sending spam
officialReferences.covers: Recorded from the team4 research files (read 2026-11-03 or 2026-11-04), not reopened: marketing messages need consent, and consent should be recorded; each message identifies the sender, and its unsubscribe works for 30 days and is honoured within five working days. Does not mention one-to-one messages.
